objective:
Add core-data's production database factory, a reusable migration test harness, and a guard that fails the build if destructive migration fallback is ever configured. Also tighten one rule in the existing DAO guard test.

CONTEXT: core-data (package root com.mcfrenchpants.activityledger.core.data). ActivityLedgerDatabase (core.data.db, internal, version 1, exportSchema, schema JSON at core-data/schemas/com.mcfrenchpants.activityledger.core.data.db.ActivityLedgerDatabase/1.json). Six tables: raw_captures, canonical_activities, activity_aliases, interpretations, activity_occurrences, corrections (13 NO ACTION foreign keys; unique activity_occurrences.raw_capture_id; unique (canonical_activity_id, normalized_alias)). Blocking DAOs; LedgerWriteDao (abstract @Dao, protected primitives, @Transaction acceptInterpretation/applyCorrection); ActivityLedgerWriter facade in core.data.ledger. Tests: Robolectric sdk=35, @RunWith(AndroidJUnit4::class), org.junit.Test + kotlin.test; inMemoryTestDatabase<T>(); test raw-SQL fixture helpers FixtureSql.kt (on SupportSQLiteDatabase) and Fixtures.kt; DaoWriteSurfaceGuardTest reads CLASS-retention Room annotations from compiled class files via test-only ClassFileAnnotations.kt. MigrationTestHelper MUST use the driver-based constructor MigrationTestHelper(instrumentation, file = targetContext.getDatabasePath(name), driver = AndroidSQLiteDriver(), databaseClass = ActivityLedgerDatabase::class) - the Instrumentation/Class constructor fails on Windows; its connections are androidx.sqlite.SQLiteConnection and do NOT enable foreign keys automatically (enable them explicitly where a test relies on enforcement). Schema JSON is exposed to tests as assets already.

WORK:
1. Production factory (internal, e.g. core.data.db.ActivityLedgerDatabaseFactory): a single place that builds the real on-disk database (fixed database file name, e.g. activity_ledger.db, overridable for tests) with an explicit migrations list (currently empty, declared as the one list both production and tests use) and no destructive fallback of any kind. No logging, no callbacks that touch row contents. It is not wired into app-phone in this task.
2. Reusable migration harness in the test source set: given a start version and a version-specific seed (raw SQL executed on the SQLiteConnection that MigrationTestHelper.createDatabase(startVersion) returns), it (a) seeds representative data covering all six tables, including at least: two raw captures with non-ASCII text (e.g. an accented word and an emoji) and a captured_zone_id; one capture with two interpretations; a NEW_ACTIVITY-created activity and an existing one; an alias; an occurrence that has been corrected, with its correction row carrying previous/new activity and time values; a HIDDEN occurrence; a MERGED activity with merged_into_activity_id set; (b) snapshots every row of all six tables (all columns, ordered by id); (c) runs runMigrationsAndValidate(currentVersion, migrations = the factory's migrations list); (d) asserts every snapshotted row still exists with identical values for every column present in both versions, foreign-key relationships still resolve (PRAGMA foreign_key_check returns no rows), and row counts match. Then (e) opens the migrated file through the production factory and reads one raw capture and one occurrence through the DAOs. The seed must use raw SQL, not current-version entities/DAOs, so it stays valid when entities change. Exercise it now for start version 1 -> current. A future migration must only need a new seed for the new start version plus one test calling the harness; show that call shape in a KDoc example.
3. Version consistency test: the current version used by the harness equals the highest N among exported core-data/schemas/<ActivityLedgerDatabase FQCN>/N.json files and equals the database's actual version (e.g. PRAGMA user_version after opening through the factory), so adding a version without an exported schema or harness run fails.
4. Destructive-fallback guard (behavioral, not only a text search): through the production factory's configuration, open a file database whose on-disk state has no migration path to the current version (e.g. a v1 database file with a marker row whose user_version is then set to a higher number so Room must downgrade, and/or any other construction you verify reaches Room's migration-required path) and assert that opening fails with Room's missing-migration error and that the marker row is still present on disk afterwards. Add a complementary source scan asserting no fallbackToDestructiveMigration* call exists in core-data/src/main. Demonstrate the behavioral guard bites: temporarily add fallbackToDestructiveMigration(dropAllTables = true) to the factory, run, capture failure; then temporarily add fallbackToDestructiveMigrationOnDowngrade(dropAllTables = true), run, capture failure; revert both. If one of those variants does not make the behavioral test fail, extend the test until it does, and report exactly what construction was needed.
5. Tighten DaoWriteSurfaceGuardTest: an UPDATE of activity_occurrences, and any @Insert whose parameter is ActivityOccurrenceEntity or CorrectionEntity, is allowed only in LedgerWriteDao; anywhere else it is a violation. Demonstrate it bites (temporarily add such a method to ActivityOccurrenceDao, capture failure, revert).
non_goals: No schema change: 1.json byte-identical, version stays 1, no entity/column/index change, no real Migration objects.
No wiring into app-phone, no dependency injection framework, no Application class changes.
No change to DAO/writer behavior beyond what the factory needs (you may add a companion constant or the migrations list).
No changes outside core-data/src (no build files, catalog, docs, other modules).
No logging of row contents; no ML Kit.
Do not disable, @Ignore or weaken existing tests or assertions.
acceptance_criteria: A production factory builds ActivityLedgerDatabase on disk with an explicit (empty) migrations list shared with the tests and no destructive fallback; `grep -rn fallbackToDestructive core-data/src/main` finds nothing.

The migration harness test for start version 1 passes, seeding all six tables with the listed representative cases via raw SQL, and asserts value-for-value survival of every row, row counts, and an empty PRAGMA foreign_key_check, then reads back through the production factory and DAOs. The harness KDoc shows how a future start version is added.
A test ties the harness's current version to the highest exported schema JSON number and to the database's actual opened version.

The behavioral destructive-fallback guard passes now and was shown to fail for both fallbackToDestructiveMigration(dropAllTables = true) and fallbackToDestructiveMigrationOnDowngrade(dropAllTables = true), with captured failure output for each; the temporary changes are absent from the final diff. A source-scan test also exists.

DaoWriteSurfaceGuardTest now rejects occurrence UPDATEs and occurrence/correction @Inserts outside LedgerWriteDao, passes on the current code, and was shown to fail with a temporary violating method in ActivityOccurrenceDao (captured output), then reverted.

core-data/schemas unchanged (git diff HEAD -- core-data/schemas empty); no Room/KSP warnings; `./gradlew :core-data:test --rerun-tasks` and `./gradlew test` pass with per-class JUnit XML counts reported; nothing changed outside core-data/src.
